body:
## Pull request overview

This PR integrates discussion/collaboration features (comments, reactions, threading) into the drawer overlay in ObjectView, ensuring the ChatterPanel is accessible regardless of how users view record details. The changes also modify the default navigation behavior to favor full-page detail views over drawer overlays.

**Changes:**
- Extracted drawer content rendering into a new `DrawerDetailContent` component with full comment data fetching and persistence
- Added `RecordChatterPanel` to drawer overlays with collapsible UI (default collapsed)
- Changed default `detailNavigation` mode from `'drawer'` to `'page'`

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 9 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ObjectView.tsx | Added DrawerDetailContent component with comment fetching/handlers; integrated RecordChatterPanel; changed default navigation from drawer to page |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ObjectView.test.tsx | Added tests for default page navigation and ChatterPanel rendering in drawer mode |

The test expects to find a button with aria-label 'Show discussion' (lowercase 'd'). However, according to RecordChatterPanel.tsx line 160, the actual aria-label is 'Show discussion' (lowercase). Verify this test actually passes - there may be a case sensitivity issue or the actual component behavior differs from expectations.
```suggestion
            const showBtn = screen.getByLabelText(/Show discussion/i);
```

This is a breaking change in default behavior. Previously, clicking a record row would open a drawer overlay by default. Now it navigates to a full page. This could significantly impact existing deployments and user workflows. Consider:
1. Adding a migration guide in CHANGELOG.md explaining the change
2. Documenting how to restore the previous drawer behavior (set navigation: { mode: 'drawer' } in object or view config)
3. Potentially adding a global configuration option to set the system-wide default
4. Ensuring this change is clearly communicated in the PR description and release notes
```suggestion
    // Priority: activeView.navigation > objectDef.navigation > default drawer
    const detailNavigation: ViewNavigationConfig = activeView?.navigation ?? objectDef.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };
```

The dataSource.find() call uses .catch(() => {}) which silently swallows all errors. If the API call fails due to network issues, authentication problems, or server errors, users won't see any feedback. Consider:
1. Logging errors to console for debugging
2. Setting an error state that can be displayed in the UI
3. Using toast notifications to inform users of failures
The same issue exists in all three handlers (handleAddComment, handleAddReply, handleToggleReaction) which use .catch(() => {}) on lines 128, 163, and 193. Consistent error handling across all these operations would improve user experience.

The test imports DetailView and RecordChatterPanel from '@object-ui/plugin-detail' via ObjectView.tsx, but there are no corresponding vi.mock declarations for this module in the test file. The test assumes these components will render actual DOM elements (like buttons with aria-label 'Show discussion'). Either add explicit mocks for '@object-ui/plugin-detail' to control the test behavior, or ensure the test environment properly loads the real components. Without mocks, this test may be flaky or fail if the actual component behavior changes.

The $filter string uses simple string concatenation with user-controlled values (threadId derived from objectDef.name and recordId). While this appears to use OData syntax, if objectDef.name or recordId contain single quotes or special characters, this could lead to injection vulnerabilities. Consider using parameterized queries or proper escaping/validation of these values before building the filter string. The same issue exists in RecordDetailView.tsx (line 52), so a shared solution would be ideal.

This comment data-fetching logic is duplicated from RecordDetailView.tsx (lines 52-75). The two implementations are almost identical. Consider extracting this into a shared custom hook like `useRecordComments(dataSource, objectName, recordId, currentUser)` to maintain single responsibility and reduce duplication. This will make future bug fixes and enhancements easier to maintain consistently across both components.

This handleAddComment logic is duplicated from RecordDetailView.tsx (lines 77-102). Consider extracting comment-related handlers (handleAddComment, handleAddReply, handleToggleReaction) into a shared custom hook like `useCommentHandlers(dataSource, objectName, recordId, currentUser)`. This would eliminate 120+ lines of duplicated code and ensure consistent behavior between the drawer and page views.
